# Authenticate Fleet HTTP ingress and bind viewer identity

## Context

Surface S1 from the graduated [Fleet Manager design record D#15249](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/15249) requires explicit operator/control-plane viewer admission for cross-inbox reads. #15269 landed the fail-closed mailbox adapter, and #15316 / PR #15312 land the read seam plus cockpit view while deliberately leaving the production source unwired.

The missing last mile is a trustworthy browser-to-Fleet request boundary. Until that boundary exists, wiring the real mailbox source would turn ambient local reachability into `CAN_READ_INBOX_OF` authority.

Live duplicate sweep: latest 20 open issues, 50 most recently updated open issues, broader GraphQL search, and the latest 30 all-state A2A messages checked at 2026-07-16T22:59Z. No equivalent active ticket exists. Closest precedents (#15185, #13172, #14988, #15283) own different boundaries.

## The Problem

At PR #15312 head `f624d5fb32`:

- [`fleetBridgeServer.mjs`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/f624d5fb32f77fb4f28357bb2469bc4231d60c1e/ai/services/fleet/fleetBridgeServer.mjs#L5-L74) is loopback-only but unauthenticated, emits wildcard CORS, reads the request body, and dispatches without a trust context.
- [`installFleetBridge.mjs`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/f624d5fb32f77fb4f28357bb2469bc4231d60c1e/src/ai/fleet/installFleetBridge.mjs#L21-L29) sends only `Content-Type`.
- [`dispatchFleetRequest.mjs`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/f624d5fb32f77fb4f28357bb2469bc4231d60c1e/ai/services/fleet/dispatchFleetRequest.mjs#L24-L31) forwards `{method, params}` directly to the bridge.
- [`FLEET_WIRE_METHODS`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/f624d5fb32f77fb4f28357bb2469bc4231d60c1e/src/ai/fleet/fleetWireMethods.mjs#L24-L27) includes lifecycle, registry, tenant, and credential-bearing operations—not merely read-only mailbox traffic.
- [`fleetMailboxMirrorAdapter.mjs`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/f624d5fb32f77fb4f28357bb2469bc4231d60c1e/ai/services/fleet/fleetMailboxMirrorAdapter.mjs#L5-L65) correctly refuses to claim admission without a bound request identity.
- The shipped `getBootIdentity`, `fleetActivity`, and `fleetRoster` JSDoc carries the same false present-tense “authenticated registryBridge” claim. Their behavior remains in scope; their prose must stop asserting a transport state that does not exist.

Loopback reachability is not authentication. Bearer possession is not viewer identity. A browser-supplied viewer id is not authority.

## The Architectural Reality

- `RequestContextService.run()` is the existing per-request identity propagation boundary. Its identity must originate at transport authentication, not from forwarded identity headers or request params.
- `MailboxService.listMessages()` already enforces `CAN_READ_INBOX_OF` against the bound canonical identity. The Fleet adapter must consume that authority; it must not recreate it.
- #15185 is reusable transport precedent, not a duplicate: its local MCP bearer proves possession only and deliberately creates no identity.
- ADR 0019 governs any required AiConfig leaves: declarative provider-owned leaves, read at the use site; no env re-derivation, pass-along aliases, runtime mutation, or hidden defaults.
- ADR 0026 §2.7 keeps the client-reachable Fleet `restartAgent` surface distinct from daemon-core L0 lifecycle authority. Authenticating the Fleet UI must not grant or imply that L0 envelope.

## The Fix

Implement one atomic Fleet ingress trust boundary:

1. The cockpit launch/bootstrap path generates one process-lifetime secret from exactly 32 cryptographically random bytes, encoded as unpadded base64url. It reaches the Fleet server and browser runtime without URL, request body, log, file, database, or durable-config persistence.
2. Fleet binds to literal loopback and independently enforces bounded Host validation, an exact cockpit-Origin policy, and constant-time bearer verification **before body parsing or dispatch**.
3. Fleet resolves the viewer independently at trusted server bootstrap, binds it to one canonical `AgentIdentity`, and rejects caller-authored identity headers or params. The bearer establishes possession of the local Fleet session; it never becomes the identity fact.
4. Every accepted request executes inside `RequestContextService.run({userId, username, agentIdentityNodeId, source}, callback)` with that server-stamped viewer. Concurrent requests remain isolated.
5. Only after steps 1–4 are proven, wire `mailboxMirrorSource` to the real `MailboxService.listMessages` path plus a dynamic `RequestContextService.getAgentIdentityNodeId()` resolver. `FleetControlBridge` remains dependency-injected and authors no admission fact.
6. The one-command Fleet boot/probe path carries the same authenticated contract. An unknown, stale, or mismatched process receives a named refusal; it is never silently reused.
7. Any new configuration surface follows ADR 0019 and remains secret-safe. Runtime code never mutates the shared AiConfig provider.

Bearer auth, viewer binding, request context, source wiring, and boot handoff remain one lane: every partial combination is either unusable or spoofable.

| Local Fleet session | Cockpit bootstrap | One 32-byte random unpadded-base64url bearer shared in memory only | Missing/malformed/mismatched bearer → 401 | Launch contract | Non-observability + negative probes |
| Viewer identity | RequestContext identity authority + #15269 | Independently server-resolved canonical `AgentIdentity`; never browser-authored | Unbound/stale identity → startup or request refusal | Binding JSDoc | spoof/unbound/canonicalization battery |
| Fleet dispatch | `FLEET_WIRE_METHODS` | Every verb runs only after transport and identity gates | No dispatch and zero side effects | Dispatcher JSDoc | mutation/credential-verb negatives |
| Request scope | `RequestContextService.run()` | Server-stamped viewer per accepted request | No context → no bridge call | Transport JSDoc | delayed concurrent A/B isolation |
| Mailbox mirror source | #15269 + #15270 | Real MailboxService read using dynamic bound viewer | Remains honestly unwired/degraded | Source JSDoc | grant/deny/cross-subject e2e |
| Existing-process probe | One-command Fleet boot contract | Authenticated identity-aware liveness/ownership check | Named mismatch; no ambient reuse | Launch docs/JSDoc | stale/wrong-token/wrong-viewer probes |

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0019 and ADR 0026`; no amendment. This consumes the existing config SSOT and request-context identity authority while preserving the Fleet UI versus daemon-core L0 envelope distinction.

## Decision Record

`NOT_NEEDED` — the graduated S1 record and existing ADRs already fix the trust boundaries; this ticket composes them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fleet startup fails closed unless the listener is literal loopback, a valid process-lifetime bearer exists, and the server-side viewer resolves to one canonical `AgentIdentity`.
- [ ] The launch path generates exactly 32 random bytes, encodes unpadded base64url, and supplies the one-run value to server and browser without URL, body, logger, SQLite, file, durable-config, or PR/test artifact persistence.
- [ ] Missing, malformed, wrong, and length-mismatched bearer values return 401 before request-body parsing, method lookup, or Fleet dispatch.
- [ ] Host validation remains independently enforced. Foreign/null Origin values are rejected; the exact cockpit Origin is echoed with `Vary: Origin`; wildcard CORS is removed. An absent Origin is accepted only with the valid bearer.
- [ ] The browser client sends `Authorization: Bearer …` and sends no viewer-identity claim.
- [ ] Authentication gates the complete `FLEET_WIRE_METHODS` surface. Negative tests prove unauthenticated lifecycle, registry, tenant, and credential-bearing calls produce zero side effects.
- [ ] The server derives `userId`, `username`, and `agentIdentityNodeId` independently of request data, then wraps every admitted call in `RequestContextService.run()`.
- [ ] A delayed concurrent viewer A/B falsifier proves request context cannot leak or swap across requests.
- [ ] `mailboxMirrorSource` is wired only after the trust boundary is active, using the dynamic bound-identity resolver and real `MailboxService.listMessages`.
- [ ] End-to-end evidence covers: admitted read, named `CAN_READ_INBOX_OF` denial, unbound viewer, spoofed viewer input, cross-subject refusal, pagination, and an unauthenticated call that never reaches MailboxService.
- [ ] The one-command boot/probe path proves correct-token/correct-viewer reuse and named refusal for stale, unknown, wrong-token, or wrong-viewer processes.
- [ ] JSDoc and operator-facing docs describe the actual trust state. The false present-tense “authenticated registryBridge” claims are removed from the staged mailbox seam and the already-shipped `getBootIdentity`, `fleetActivity`, and `fleetRoster` verbs; no site asserts authentication before this boundary is live.
- [ ] Any AiConfig additions satisfy ADR 0019 at the use site; tests isolate by construction and never mutate the shared provider.
- [ ] Focused unit, integration, and Neural Link evidence covers the full browser → HTTP → RequestContext → MailboxService admission path.

## Out of Scope

- Remote/cloud Fleet hosting, multi-tenant authentication, GitHub PAT/OAuth/OIDC productization.
- Legacy HTTP+SSE support.
- Broad Fleet authorization redesign or changing ADR 0026 daemon-core L0 authority.
- Mailbox mutation, reply-as-operator, archive browsing, or mark-read.
- Visual redesign beyond the minimal authenticated client plumbing.

## Avoided Traps

- Treating loopback, Host, Origin, or bearer possession individually as viewer identity.
- Accepting a browser-authored `viewerIdentity`, forwarded identity header, or fixed request param.
- Wiring MailboxService before a request-bound identity exists.
- Protecting only `fleetMailboxMirror` while leaving credential/lifecycle verbs ambient.
- Reusing #15185’s possession token as an authorization grant.
- Splitting the trust boundary into mergeable partial tickets whose intermediate state is unsafe.

Loopback reachability is not authentication, bearer possession is not viewer
identity, and a browser-supplied viewer id is not authority. This commit makes
all three false by construction at the transport layer:

- fleetIngressAuth.mjs: one pure admission guard, cheapest-reject-first —
  exact Host allowlist (port included, resolved at listen time so ephemeral
  ports stay honest), exact cockpit-Origin policy (foreign and literal-null
  refused; the request's own origin echoed only after matching, always with
  Vary: Origin), then the constant-time bearer check via the shared
  localBearer primitives. Preflights admit on Host+Origin alone because
  OPTIONS cannot carry Authorization; they read no body and dispatch nothing.

- fleetBridgeServer.mjs: fail-closed construction (no canonical bearer, no
  bound viewer, no context runner => synchronous refusal, no listener exists);
  the guard runs BEFORE a body byte is read — refused requests never attach
  data listeners, are answered with Connection: close, and drain unparsed.
  Every admitted POST /fleet executes inside the injected request-context
  runner with the SERVER-stamped viewer — a caller-authored identity field
  never enters the flow. Wildcard CORS is gone. GET /fleet/probe (bearer-
  gated) answers the boot contract with identity facts, never the credential.

- installFleetBridge.mjs (client half): sends Authorization: Bearer from an
  in-memory argument; refuses credential-shaped query params on the fleet URL
  outright; without a bearer it installs FAIL-CLOSED — every call rejects
  locally with the launch-contract remediation and zero network traffic.
  apps/agentos boot reads the bearer from the in-memory injection slot only,
  never from URL params.

across lifecycle/registry/tenant/credential verbs; spoofed-Host; foreign and

durability is the contract, a late wake is noise.

Evidence: L2 — unit specs for the compose surface (wake inversion, isValid gate, intent shape) and

cockpitDockDocument + projection guards hold (their superset / existence / zero-placeholder
assertions are unaffected by the additive auto-hidden item). CI is the oracle for the agentos shard.

Remaining (controller wiring on this branch as the server halves land): recipientOptions fed from
the live FleetRoster; compose -> the Brain compose verb via the authenticated registryBridge; the
operator inbox snapshot + paged re-read via the ingress viewer identity.

Refs #15377, #15376, #15320

* feat(agentos): wire the FM operator-mailbox controller — compose + recipientOptions + inbox read scaffold (#15377)

The cockpit composition root now services the operator-mailbox surface's intents: onOperatorCompose routes to the authenticated composeOperatorMessage write verb (sender server-stamped, never wire-carried) and re-polls the inbox at canonical truth; onOperatorInboxPageRequest re-reads the own-inbox mirror. Adds composeOperatorMessage + buildOperatorRecipientOptions (roster identity map + AGENT:* sentinel) + loadOperatorInbox (generation-fenced, fail-closed, own-inbox twin of AgentDetail.loadMailboxMirror). resolveDockComponentRef feeds record/snapshot/recipientOptions + wires the compose/inboxPageRequest listeners. The own-inbox subjectAgentId resolution (viewer identity) is confirmed with the ingress owner before the initial read + identity load land.

* test(agentos): cover the FM operator-mailbox seam — compose, recipients, fail-closed inbox (#15377)

12 unit specs for the three composition-root methods wired in 61f9c60fd8, on the same
prototype.call(fakeCockpit) harness as the loadActivity block (no full instantiation):

- composeOperatorMessage: not-wired refusal (no bridge / no verb, nothing attempted);
  the payload reaches the verb UNCHANGED on a real send (frozen input + fresh-literal
  assertion, so an injected sender field would fail) with a single offset-0 re-read;
  and a rejected outcome (no messageId) re-reads nothing.
- buildOperatorRecipientOptions: the live roster maps to @githubUsername identities,
  NOT the agentId key (the fixture makes the two fields differ so the wrong read fails),
  plus the AGENT:* broadcast sentinel; a row with no mailbox identity drops.
- loadOperatorInbox: the fail-closed matrix (no identity / no verb → honestly unobserved,
  the read attempt still advances the generation) plus BOTH fences — a superseded
  generation and a destroyed owner never write — and a throwing verb keeps last-known.

* fix(agentos): operator-compose priority defaults to HIGH (AC-7) + repair the mailbox specs my mount left red (#15377)

The compose priority default was 'normal', contradicting AC-7's "priority-high default":
operator steering ranks first at the recipient's turn-start drain — paired with the wake-off
default it reads "top of your queue when you next look, but I won't interrupt you now". Fixed
the field default and the onSendClick fallback; the spec proves it on the fired intent (the
real contract), not the ComboBox's `.value` record.

Repairs to specs my own f93fa2da03 shipped without running (all unpushed, none had hit CI):
- operatorMailbox / operatorComposeForm: add the `import Instance` that registers Neo.get — the
  Chip/ComboBox fields build a source-bound collection whose afterSetSourceId calls it, so
  without it the specs crash in isolation (green only when a shared-worker sibling imported it
  first). Mirrors fleetCockpit.spec's robust import.
- operatorMailbox: a fired `source` is stamped as the component id, not the instance — assert
  box.id (the owner resolves it via Neo.getComponent); and the shipped MailboxPane clones its
  snapshot config, so assert deep-equal, not reference.
- fleetCockpitPopOut (#14610): my cockpit mount added the 'operator' rail tab to secondary-rail,
  so the exact-index reattach assertions now include it — the detail->index-0 invariant still holds.

Full fleet unit dir: 274 passed (from 4 red at baseline).

* feat(agentos): wire the operator-mailbox boot trigger — resolveViewerIdentity → own-inbox read (#15377)

The last slice of the FM operator-mailbox, unblocked by resolveViewerIdentity landing on dev
(PR #15418). The mirror read requires an EXPLICIT subjectAgentId — never a viewer-default, since
a self-default at a trust boundary is spoof-adjacent — so the cockpit had no way to read the
operator's OWN inbox: it did not know its own @-id. resolveViewerIdentity (whoami) is that missing
bootstrap leg of "the client SAYS self, the admission stamp proves it".

- FleetCockpit.loadOperatorIdentity(): calls the authenticated bridge's resolveViewerIdentity()
  (no params) → {ok, agentIdentityNodeId} → seeds operatorRecord owner-side → pushes it to the pane.
  Fail-closed on both refusal shapes (source-not-wired / unbound) and on an absent bridge: the pane
  stays honestly unobserved, never a fabricated or fallback identity. Wired into onConstructed.
- OperatorMailbox.afterSetRecord: a newly-bound identity (null → record) fires the initial
  inboxPageRequest(offset 0), so a pane materialized after boot lands its inbox without a page
  gesture — exactly as AgentDetail reads on its record. Single read-path: the pane holds "I have a
  record → read", the cockpit holds the read mechanism.

Read paths: boot-visible → the pushed record fires the read; revealed-later → projection materializes
the pane at the held identity, which fires the read. Both flow through the generation-fenced
loadOperatorInbox.

6 new witnesses: resolveViewerIdentity ok → seed + pane-push; no-verb / ok:false refusal → fail-closed
no seed; autoHidden-at-boot still seeds for reveal; afterSetRecord fires the read on a real identity and
NOT on a null clear. Full fleet unit dir: 280 passed.

* fix(agentos): operator-mailbox possession — seed record.githubUsername so the own inbox renders (#15377)

Review RA-1 (possession), the P1 falsifier: MailboxPane's possession guard
(`isSnapshotForThisSubject`) canonicalizes `record.githubUsername` to `@<username>` and
matches it against the mirror admission's `subjectAgentId`. `loadOperatorIdentity` seeded only
`{agentIdentityNodeId}`, so `record.githubUsername` was undefined → the guard failed CLOSED and
the operator's own inbox never rendered, despite green units.

Now the record carries both: `githubUsername` (the possession authority) derived from the
resolved `@`-form node id, and the node id as the explicit read subject — they canonicalize to
the same value, so the admission the mirror stamps matches. Tests use a realistic `@`-form
identity (not a `NODE:` placeholder) and assert the possession field.

Partial: this is RA-1's possession leg. The reveal-lifecycle propagation, the real recipient
contract (RA-2), the async outcome loop (RA-3), honest AC-4 (RA-4), real-component + falsifier
witnesses, and the browser-gated live-FM journey + design sign-off (RA-5) remain — #15427 stays
CHANGES_REQUESTED until it is a working product.

* fix(agentos): operator-mailbox reveal lifecycle — flush projection-injected state to the children (#15377)

Review RA-1 (reveal half), the second falsifier: `afterSetRecord`/`afterSetSnapshot`/
`afterSetRecipientOptions` all return early while `!isConstructed`, so state supplied as
CONSTRUCTION configs — the normal reveal-after-boot path, when the cockpit already holds the
resolved operator identity/snapshot/options — never reached the children. The pane materialized
EMPTY and could not pass possession.

`onConstructed` now flushes `record`/`snapshot`/`recipientOptions` to the inbox pane + compose
form, then a construction-time identity kicks its first read (afterSetRecord was skipped
pre-construct, so this is the single fire for the reveal path).

Tested on the REAL composed component (not a spy / not post-construction assignment, per the
review): a box constructed with injected configs has its children carrying that state. With
RA-1's possession seeding (f33d8de67f), the operator's own inbox now renders on reveal. Full
fleet dir: 281 passed.

* feat(agentos): operator-compose fan-out — several recipients, one authenticated call each, per-target outcomes (#15377)

RA-2/RA-3 controller half (Euclid's standing RC on #15427). The compose verb is
one-target, so the cockpit fans out: each named recipient is a separate
authenticated call carrying its OWN outcome (sent | not-wired | rejected | error),
AGENT:* stays one call (server-expanded), a scalar 'to' stays back-compatible.
Thrown bridge promises are caught per-recipient (no detached rejection); the inbox
re-polls exactly once per batch, only when a real send landed. Uniform return
{results:[{to,outcome}]}. New discriminating witness: several recipients, one sent
+ one rejected — a shape a single aggregate verdict cannot produce. 20 fleetCockpit
specs green. Next increment: the form-side multi-select recipient + the outcome
response-seam that renders per-target state (the current fire-and-forget still
drops it — Observable.fire).

* feat(agentos): operator-compose recipient picker — real multi-select over the roster (#15377)

RA-2 form-side (Euclid's standing RC on #15427). The single-select ChipField
collapsed its value to one scalar (Chip/ComboBox getSelection()[0]) and could not
express several peers; replaced with a real list.Base(singleSelect:false) over the

required (the gate lives in onSendClick since the list carries no field-level
required), and the options stay current across roster load/reconciliation.

* feat(agentos): operator-compose outcome loop — per-recipient verdicts render, no refusal is invisible (#15377)

RA-3 form-side / the outcome response-seam (Euclid's P1: refusal/failure states
invisible). The form fires compose intent-only and Observable.fire discards handler
returns, so the fan-out {results} could never reach the UI. Now the controller
awaits the settled outcome and writes it BACK onto the operator-mailbox surface,
which relays it to the compose form; the form renders one row PER recipient (sent /
not-wired / rejected / error) plus a pending line on send. Closes the loop: a
refusal or failure is visible, per-recipient, never collapsed to one verdict.

the controller write-back loop-closer. 290 fleet specs green. Completes RA-2+RA-3
as the coherent unit; RA-4 (AC-4 scope) + RA-5 (rebase/browser journey) remain.
